canonical_claim: For fixed-cut bipartite pure-state dynamics, standard spectrum-based entanglement measures are nonlinear projections of one Schmidt-spectrum path. Across the tested dynamical families, three non-equivalent metric classes share a dominant exact-boundary-normalized trajectory mode and preserve substantial relational morphology. The preservation is hierarchical rather than exact, and local contradictions occur on majorization-incomparable spectral steps. This supports an empirical metric-robust trajectory class, not a formal topological invariant or universal individual-run fingerprint.

claims.statement: For a declared bipartition of a pure state, the Schmidt-spectrum path is the ordered reduced-density-matrix spectrum as a function of time.
claims.scope: fixed-cut bipartite pure-state dynamics

claims.statement: The entanglement-trajectory atlas is the family of time-ordered projections obtained by applying declared spectrum functionals to one Schmidt-spectrum path.
claims.scope: declared metric family and bipartition

claims.statement: At fixed largest Schmidt value, the concentrated spectrum majorizes every compatible spectrum and every compatible spectrum majorizes the equal-tail spectrum.
claims.scope: finite-dimensional ordered probability spectra with fixed maximum entry

claims.statement: The majorization extremizers give exact finite-dimensional fixed-largest-eigenvalue envelopes for the declared Schur-concave metric families.
claims.scope: metric families and domains listed in metadata/metric_registry.json

claims.statement: Majorization-compatible spectrum pairs are ordered consistently by every Schur-concave entropy in the declared family.
claims.scope: nonnegative Renyi orders and equivalent Schur-concave quantities under their stated conventions

claims.statement: For bipartite pure states, logarithmic negativity equals the Renyi-one-half entropy.
claims.scope: bipartite pure states

claims.statement: Linear entropy, purity, Renyi-two entropy, participation ratio, I-concurrence, and I-tangle contain overlapping or strictly transformed information and must not be counted as independent metric families.
claims.scope: definitions and normalizations in the metric registry

claims.statement: Hartley entropy uses exact represented support: H0=log rank. At fixed largest Schmidt value p, the minimum rank is ceil(1/p), and the maximum is d for p<1 and one for p=1.
claims.scope: finite-dimensional validated spectra; thresholded numerical rank is excluded from this claim
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not identify a threshold-dependent numerical rank with exact Hartley entropy.

claims.statement: The exact-boundary-normalized common metric mode explains 90.2628 percent of total standardized variance.

uncertainty.interpretation: Sensitivity interval over the 16 designed model-condition clusters, stratified by model; not a population interval over independently sampled disorder or initial-state ensembles.

claims.scope: three vertical metric classes, 96 included trajectories, four model families, six sizes
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not call this exact metric equivalence or a universal invariant.

claims.statement: The median trajectory-level common-mode fraction is 94.7514 percent.
claims.scope: 96 included trajectories

claims.statement: Boundary-normalized within-trajectory rank agreement ranges from 0.6922 to 0.9473 across the three tested metric pairs.
claims.scope: cluster means over the 16 model-condition runs

claims.statement: Metric competition occurs on 808 of 5,760 consecutive scalar steps in the designed trajectory table.
claims.scope: all included scalar trajectories and the three tested vertical metric classes

claims.statement: All 50 metric-competition events in the selected complete-spectrum audit occur among majorization-incomparable transitions, with zero outside that sector.
claims.scope: five selected n=20 runs and 400 consecutive spectrum transitions
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Incomparability permits disagreement but does not force it.

claims.statement: Metric competition is model dependent in the supplied data.
claims.scope: included scalar trajectories

claims.statement: Exact vertical turn counts agree across all three tested metrics on only 2 of 96 trajectories.
claims.scope: sampling and turn-count convention documented in docs/ANALYSIS_METHODS.md
claims.implication: Fine projected path structure is not invariant.

claims.statement: Gap-aware model-centroid full-path classification with held-out size reaches 0.875 same-metric accuracy and 0.6736 cross-metric accuracy; vertical-only transfer is weaker, and individual size-plus-condition holdout remains preliminary.
claims.scope: nearest-centroid stress tests documented in docs/ANALYSIS_METHODS.md

claims.statement: The dominant boundary-normalized common mode persists under equal-trajectory weighting, within-trajectory standardization, first-difference analysis, leave-one-model-out analysis, and separate-size fits.
claims.scope: Sensitivity analyses of the same deterministic designed dataset; not independent experimental replication.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not describe these reformulations as independent datasets or population replication.

claims.statement: The project has not proved a formal topological invariant.
claims.scope: all public interpretation

claims.statement: The current evidence does not establish a universal individual-run fingerprint.
claims.scope: classification claims

claims.statement: The central claim does not cover every entanglement notion, mixed-state entanglement, or genuine multipartite invariants.
claims.scope: fixed-cut pure-state construction

claims.statement: The published three-curve region is an approximate outer arena rather than the exact tight boundary.
The published Page expression is asymptotic rather than the exact finite-dimensional complex-Haar mean.
claims.replacement: Use the harmonic-number formula documented in the correction layer.

claims.statement: The deterministic mean component of the noncentral Wishart construction is rank one.
claims.replacement: It has one nonzero eigenvalue and all remaining eigenvalues zero.

claims.statement: A global quantum Fourier transform does not generally preserve the Schmidt spectrum.
claims.replacement: Describe the paper overlap as state-family-specific numerical behavior and retain the explicit counterexample.

claims.statement: Random-matrix constructions provide conditional references, not the exact feasible boundary or a universal attractor.
The released random-field XXZ rows are fixed one-substep symmetric product-formula circuits, not convergence-controlled continuous-time XXZ Hamiltonian trajectories.
claims.scope: All released XXZ rows; convergence audit at n=10,12,14.

claims.statement: The trajectory table is a deterministic designed dataset with four conditions per model, not an independent ensemble of population draws.
claims.scope: All bootstrap and classification statements.

claims.statement: The 400-transition majorization audit uses five selected n=20 runs and is a mechanism check, not a model-wide frequency estimate.
claims.scope: Selected full-spectrum audit only.

required_nonclaims: A formal topological invariant has been proved.
Every entanglement notion is a function of one fixed Schmidt spectrum.
Random matrix theory supplies the exact boundary.
All tested dynamics converge to a random-matrix attractor.
Entropy magnitude alone certifies simulation cost, computational usefulness, or quantum advantage.
The current atlas is a universal individual-run classifier.
All named metrics in the package are independent.
A threshold-dependent numerical Schmidt rank is not the exact Hartley entropy.
